---
title: "Concepts"
subtitle: "Learnings and issues, weights, scopes, and the git-native store."
---

## The base skill is the architecture; Whetstone is the weights

> A skill is the **architecture** — shared, tested, canonical, the same for everyone. Whetstone is
> the **weights** — everything learned about *your* preferences, layered on at runtime and never
> baked into the skill.

Whetstone never modifies the skill. It keeps a separate, per-skill memory and applies it at the
start of each run, so your taste can evolve — and even run against the skill's defaults — without
mutating something everyone shares.

## Learnings vs. issues

Every entry Whetstone stores has a **polarity**:

```{=html}
<div class="ws-cards" style="margin-top:1.25rem;">
  <div class="ws-card">
    <div class="ws-card-icon">≈</div>
    <h3 class="ws-card-title">Learning</h3>
    <p class="ws-card-body">A soft, weighted, decaying <strong>preference</strong> — what you like.
      "Negatives in parentheses", "warm palette, not green", "square corners." Retrieved by
      relevance and applied as taste.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="ws-card">
    <div class="ws-card-icon">!</div>
    <h3 class="ws-card-title">Issue</h3>
    <p class="ws-card-body">A hard, mandatory <strong>rule</strong> the skill must never repeat — an
      explicit "always / never." Not subject to decay; treated as a constraint, not a suggestion.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

A correction becomes a *learning* when it's taste, and an *issue* when it's an "always/never" or a
mistake to never repeat. `capture` classifies and words it; `revise` can `promote` a preference into
a rule or `demote` a rule back to a preference later.

## Weight, decay, and recurrence

Learnings carry a **weight** that captures how strongly a preference is held. Repeating a correction
(`revise … reinforce`) raises it; contradicting one (`weaken`) lowers it; unused learnings **decay**
over time so stale taste fades instead of accumulating forever. This trajectory is exactly what the
**[Metrics → value-over-time](metrics.qmd)** view plots. Issues are mandatory and don't decay.

## Scopes

Entries are grouped by **scope** — a short slug describing *what* the preference is about (e.g.
`currency-formatting`, `color-palette`). Scoping is what makes retrieval precise: `recall` matches
your elaborated intent against scopes, so a table-styling task surfaces table-styling preferences and
nothing else. It's also why passing a rich, elaborated `intent` to `recall` matters so much.

## Storage & config {#storage-config}

Each skill's learned layer is its **own git repository** under the XDG data dir (default
`~/.local/share/whetstone/<skill-slug>/`; override with `WHETSTONE_STORE_ROOT` or `store_root` in
config):

```default
<store-root>/<skill-slug>/
  learnings/<scope-slug>.md   your preferences, grouped by scope (source of truth)
  issues/<scope-slug>.md      hard rules, grouped by scope (source of truth)
  next_ids.json               per-store id counters (git-tracked; prevents id reuse)
  index.sqlite                derived embedding cache (rebuildable, git-ignored)
  events.jsonl                per-run telemetry for metrics (git-ignored)
  .git/                       full version history of the markdown
```

The markdown is the **source of truth** — read it, edit it, `git revert` it. The SQLite index and
the event log are derived and git-ignored. Nothing leaves your machine.

Configuration is read from `~/.config/whetstone/config.toml`, and every key also has a
`WHETSTONE_*` environment override. The most common one is the recall backend:

```toml
# ~/.config/whetstone/config.toml
embedding_backend = "sentence-transformers"   # default: "hashing" (deterministic, dependency-free)
```

The default `hashing` backend needs no extra dependencies and no network. The
`sentence-transformers` backend (install the `embeddings` extra — see **[Install](install.qmd)**)
gives higher-quality, intent-aware retrieval; it's the backend this site's showcase runs on.
